title: Chavin de Huantar
subtitle: Ritual architecture, psychoactive plants, sound, and authority in the Early Horizon Andes
summary: A concise archaeological site entry on Chavin de Huantar as a ceremonial center where architecture, controlled movement, sound, San Pedro imagery, and direct evidence for vilca and Nicotiana snuff formed part of institutionalized ritual practice.
abstract: Chavin de Huantar was a major ceremonial and pilgrimage center in the northern Peruvian highlands. Its psychedelic dimensions are not based on speculative ancient-mystery literature: they rest on San Pedro cactus imagery, snuffing paraphernalia, tenon-head iconography, sensory architecture, archaeoacoustic research, and 2025 chemical and microbotanical evidence for vilca and Nicotiana residues on inhalation instruments from Gallery 3.
editorial_note: Archaeological site description compiled from UNESCO, Stanford/CyArk Chavin research, peer-reviewed work on San Pedro, vilca, Nicotiana, snuff paraphernalia, and Chavin archaeoacoustics.
citation: The Psychedelic History Archive. "Chavin de Huantar." Archaeological site entry, compiled from UNESCO World Heritage documentation and cited archaeological scholarship.
